description:
Kayla has three hours to get ready for her first date with Theo. Her roommate counts every percent and the hair dryer has opinions. Then they read the text again.

lines.text: Getting ready for a first date. Loading. Zero percent.
I am in pajamas. I have one sock on. I have never been more beautiful.
Hello. I am the hair dryer. I have not been plugged in since the wedding in June.
He picks me up at seven. That is three hours. That is plenty of time.
Last time you said plenty of time, you missed a whole birthday.
I did not miss it. I arrived for the cake. The cake is the birthday.
Loading. Four percent. She found the other sock. It was in the freezer.
Why is it always the freezer.
Okay. Hair. Today the hair is going to be big. Like a cloud with confidence.
I am ready. I have been ready for five months. Turn me on.
Loading. Eleven percent. The power went out in the bathroom.
That was me. I am sorry. I am very strong.
Half of my hair is a cloud. The other half is a wet cat.
Loading. Twenty percent. Restarting the hair.
Brooke, stop saying loading. I am a person, not a phone.
Your phone gets ready faster than you. Your phone has never tried on nine shirts.
Outfit number one. Casual. Like I did not try.
You look like you are going to return a lamp.
Outfit number two. Fancy.
She looks like a fancy lamp.
Outfit number three. Mysterious. All black. Sunglasses inside.
Loading. Forty percent. She walked into the door.
The door moved. I am fine. My mystery is fine.
Forty one. Forty two. She is doing eyeliner. Nobody breathe.
I am holding my breath. I do not even have lungs.
One eye is a cat. The other eye is a different cat.
Sixty percent. Two cats. We continue.
Perfume. Just a little.
That was not a little. I can taste it. I am a hair dryer and I can taste it.
Eighty five percent. Shoes. The hard part.
The cute shoes hurt. The comfy shoes look like two potatoes.
Wear the potatoes. Nobody looks at feet on a first date.
He might. He might be a foot guy. I do not know his life.
Ninety nine percent.
Ninety nine. Why am I stuck at ninety nine?
Everyone gets stuck at ninety nine. It is the hardest one.
One more look in the mirror. One more. One more. One more.
Still ninety nine. It has been eleven minutes.
Okay. Text him. Tell him I am ready. Tell him casually.
Opening your messages. Oh. Oh, Kayla.
What. What oh.
He says, see you Friday at seven. It is Sunday.
She is six days early. That is the most ready anyone has ever been.
No. No no no. I did two cats for nothing.
One hundred percent. With nowhere to go.
Then I will stay like this until Friday. I will sleep standing up.
Please do not. I cannot do this again on Friday. I am retired.
Hi. Sorry. Is Kayla here? I know it is not Friday.
Theo? Why are you all dressed up?
I got ready for Friday. I finished early. Like, six days early.
I have been one hundred percent since lunch. My cat is tired of looking at me.
Two people at one hundred percent. This has never happened in history.
So, do you want to go right now? It is Sunday. Places are open.
Yes. Please. My shoes hurt. These are not potatoes.
Mine are potatoes. Do you look at feet?
Only to see if they are potatoes.
Friday is cancelled. I am going back in the drawer. Good night forever.
